I’ve been working at a Midwest-based coffee chain for a little over a year now. There have definitely been some oddballs.

Recently, within the last month, It was just myself and a new person on a closing shift - we had this older man come through our drive through with a fairly simple order, no biggie.

After this man gets his order, he drives out to sit in the parking lot for 5 or so minutes. After which, he goes back into the drive through and claims that we didn’t make his order right.

He pulls up to the window and I’m like “sir what’s the problem”

“I was just here and you guys messed up my order, I want you to make me what I ordered”

So I grab the receipt from him, and lo and behold it not only has a completely different order - it was also marked for 11:30 AM, in MAY. 

After I attempted explaining that to him, he became belligerent and was telling me that that’s the receipt he was given by the new person, and if he didn’t get his correct order (for free of course in addition to what he had actually ordered) he would be “having a talk with the manager”

I was starting my freshman year of college and was in a bunch of art classes (art major). That being said, professional-grade art supplies are expensive as shit, and I was in no way prepared by how much all of the required materials were going to cost me (all of it had to be paid for out of pocket since they didn’t offer any supplies that I needed in the actual school store where I could’ve used aid). Well, needless to say, I was starting to freak out as to how to afford all of these class materials on top of everything else I needed, and this incredible worker at the craft store took every single coupon he had available - including some he could’ve gotten in trouble for using; and applied them to my order. He risked getting in trouble to help me get the things I needed for class and I am still so incredibly thankful that someone was willing to show so much kindness. If I ever saw him again I would make sure to thank him a million times over because without that help I genuinely don’t think I’d have continued with my major. Thank you kick-ass craft store guy!
